title: Dasakam 54 — Kāliyasya Kālindīprāptiḥ tathā Viṣabādhā
description: Saubhari’s curse keeps Garuda from the Kalindi; Kaliya enters its waters, whose poison harms the forest and cowherds until Krishna restores them.
translation_note: No vetted stanza translation supplied. English captions are preserved verbatim as attributed reference commentary, separate from canonical Sanskrit and IAST.

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वत्सेवोत्कः सौभरिर्नाम पूर्वं
कालिन्द्यन्तर्द्वादशाब्दं तपस्यन् ।
मीनव्राते स्नेहवान् भोगलोले
तार्क्ष्यं साक्षादैक्षताग्रे कदाचित् ॥ ५४-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvatsevotkaḥ saubharirnāma pūrvaṃ
kālindyantardvādaśābdaṃ tapasyan |
mīnavrāte snehavān bhogalole
tārkṣyaṃ sākṣādaikṣatāgre kadācit || 54-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Long ago, Saubhari sage performed penance by submerging in the waters of Kaalindi, for twelve years, to have Bhagwan’s vision. He became attached to the fish who kept living there. Once he saw Garuda right in front of his eyes.

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वद्वाहं तं सक्षुधं तृक्षसूनुं
मीनं कञ्चिज्जक्षतं लक्षयन् सः ।
तप्तश्चित्ते शप्तवानत्र चेत्त्वं
जन्तून् भोक्ता जीवितं चापि मोक्ता ॥ ५४-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadvāhaṃ taṃ sakṣudhaṃ tṛkṣasūnuṃ
mīnaṃ kañcijjakṣataṃ lakṣayan saḥ |
taptaścitte śaptavānatra cettvaṃ
jantūn bhoktā jīvitaṃ cāpi moktā || 54-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Garuda who was hungry ate a fish. Seeing that, Saubhari was very agitated and cursed Garuda saying that he would lose his life if he ate any creatures there.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तस्मिन् काले कालियः क्ष्वेलदर्पात्
सर्पारातेः कल्पितं भागमश्नन् ।
तेन क्रोधात् त्वत्पदाम्भोजभाजा
पक्षक्षिप्तस्तद्दुरापं पयोऽगात् ॥ ५४-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tasmin kāle kāliyaḥ kṣveladarpāt
sarpārāteḥ kalpitaṃ bhāgamaśnan |
tena krodhāt tvatpadāmbhojabhājā
pakṣakṣiptastaddurāpaṃ payo’gāt || 54-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: At that time, Kaaliya the serpent was full of pride due to the power of his poison. He ate away the offerings kept for Garuda.. Angered at this, Garuda who is devoted to Bhagwan attacked Kaaliya and chased him. Knowing that Garuda will not come to the river Kaalindi due to sage Shoubari's curse, Kaaliya took refuge in it.

stanzas.sanskrit:
घोरे तस्मिन् सूरजानीरवासे
तीरे वृक्षा विक्षताः क्ष्वेलवेगात् ।
पक्षिव्राताः पेतुरभ्रे पतन्तः
कारुण्यार्द्रं त्वन्मनस्तेन जातम् ॥ ५४-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ghore tasmin sūrajānīravāse
tīre vṛkṣā vikṣatāḥ kṣvelavegāt |
pakṣivrātāḥ peturabhre patantaḥ
kāruṇyārdraṃ tvanmanastena jātam || 54-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: As the cruel Kaaliya was living in the waters of Kaalindi, the trees dried up and the birds who flew in the sky above, fell down dead. Bhagwan’s heart melted in compassion and was moved with pity seeing the plight of the creatures.

stanzas.sanskrit:
काले तस्मिन्नेकदा सीरपाणिं
मुक्त्वा याते यामुनं काननान्तम् ।
त्वय्युद्दामग्रीष्मभीष्मोष्मतप्ता
गोगोपाला व्यापिबन् क्ष्वेलतोयम् ॥ ५४-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kāle tasminnekadā sīrapāṇiṃ
muktvā yāte yāmunaṃ kānanāntam |
tvayyuddāmagrīṣmabhīṣmoṣmataptā
gogopālā vyāpiban kṣvelatoyam || 54-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: On one hot summer day, Krishna went to the interior of the forest on the banks of the river Yamuna without his brother Balarama. The cows and cowherds which felt very thirsty drank the river water which was poisoned.

stanzas.sanskrit:
नश्यज्जीवान् विच्युतान् क्ष्मातले तान्
विश्वान् पश्यन्नच्युत त्वं दयार्द्रः ।
प्राप्योपान्तं जीवयामासिथ द्राक्
पीयूषाम्भोवर्षिभिः श्रीकटाक्षैः ॥ ५४-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
naśyajjīvān vicyutān kṣmātale tān
viśvān paśyannacyuta tvaṃ dayārdraḥ |
prāpyopāntaṃ jīvayāmāsitha drāk
pīyūṣāmbhovarṣibhiḥ śrīkaṭākṣaiḥ || 54-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: The cows and the Gopas soon fell dead on the ground. Krishna felt pity for the cows and Gopas and by His merciful glances, which were like showering nectar into their body, revived them back to life.

stanzas.sanskrit:
किं किं जातो हर्षवर्षातिरेकः
सर्वाङ्गेष्वित्युत्थिता गोपसङ्घाः ।
दृष्ट्वाऽग्रे त्वां त्वत्कृतं तद्विदन्त-
-स्त्वामालिङ्गन् दृष्टनानाप्रभावाः ॥ ५४-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kiṃ kiṃ jāto harṣavarṣātirekaḥ
sarvāṅgeṣvityutthitā gopasaṅghāḥ |
dṛṣṭvā’gre tvāṃ tvatkṛtaṃ tadvidanta-
-stvāmāliṅgan dṛṣṭanānāprabhāvāḥ || 54-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopas got up from ground wondering the feel of the bliss showered in their various parts of the body. They understood that is was Krishna’s divine act and hugged and thanked Krishna for saving them.

stanzas.sanskrit:
गावश्चैवं लब्धजीवाः क्षणेन
स्फीतानन्दास्त्वां च दृष्ट्वा पुरस्तात् ।
द्रागावव्रुः सर्वतो हर्षबाष्पं
व्यामुञ्चन्त्यो मन्दमुद्यन्निनादाः ॥ ५४-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gāvaścaivaṃ labdhajīvāḥ kṣaṇena
sphītānandāstvāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā purastāt |
drāgāvavruḥ sarvato harṣabāṣpaṃ
vyāmuñcantyo mandamudyanninādāḥ || 54-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Like how the Gopas felt the flow of bliss in their bodies, even the cows felt grateful and surrounded Krishna with tears of joy.

stanzas.sanskrit:
रोमाञ्चोऽयं सर्वतो नः शरीरे
भूयस्यन्तः काचिदानन्दमूर्छा ।
आश्चर्योऽयं क्ष्वेलवेगो मुकुन्दे-
-त्युक्तो गोपैर्नन्दितो वन्दितोऽभूः ॥ ५४-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
romāñco’yaṃ sarvato naḥ śarīre
bhūyasyantaḥ kācidānandamūrchā |
āścaryo’yaṃ kṣvelavego mukunde-
-tyukto gopairnandito vandito’bhūḥ || 54-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopas had goosebumps all over their body. They were experiencing bliss which could not be expressed. Wondering if it was all due to the poison, the gopas fell at Krishna's feet and praised and prayed to him.

stanzas.sanskrit:
एवं भक्तान् मुक्तजीवानपि त्वं
मुग्धापाङ्गैरस्तरोगांस्तनोषि ।
तादृग्भूतस्फीतकारुण्यभूमा
रोगात् पाया वायुगेहाधिनाथ ॥ ५४-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
evaṃ bhaktān muktajīvānapi tvaṃ
mugdhāpāṅgairastarogāṃstanoṣi |
tādṛgbhūtasphītakāruṇyabhūmā
rogāt pāyā vāyugehādhinātha || 54-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Thus Bhagwan revived his devotees by his merciful glances and rendered them devoid of any disease. Bhattathiri prayed to Lord Guruvayoorappan to protect him and release him of his disease with his merciful glances.
